definition_zh: 为什么；何以；原因；理由
definition_en: the question word for a reason, and the reason or purpose itself
core_image: 一个孩子拽着大人的袖子，抬头追问那一个问题：为什么
scene: 孩子指着天上慢慢走的云，一遍遍追问它究竟为什么不肯停下来。Why did the train stop in the middle of the field?
sceneCN: 这里 why 是「为什么」（第 1 个义项：询问原因的疑问词）；句意为火车为什么停在田野中间。孩子拽着袖子抬头追问的那一幕，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Asking for a reason
senses.definition: used at the start of a question to ask for the cause or the purpose of something
senses.definitionCN: 放在问句开头，询问某事的原因或目的
senses.example: Why did the train stop in the middle of the field?
senses.exampleCN: 火车为什么停在田野中间？
senses.why: The word asks for the thread that leads back from an event to its cause.
senses.whyCN: 这个词追问的是从一件事牵回其起因的那根线。

senses.title: In the phrase why not
senses.definition: used to suggest something or to agree cheerfully to a proposal
senses.definitionCN: 用来提议某事，或愉快地同意一个建议
senses.example: Why not take the early bus and be there before lunch?
senses.exampleCN: 何不坐早班车，午饭前就能到？
senses.why: A question turned into a gentle push, since the missing answer is obviously yes.
senses.whyCN: 一个问句变成了温和的推动，因为缺的那个答案显然是「好」。

senses.title: Introducing a clause after reason
senses.definition: used after the noun reason to introduce the clause that explains it
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词 reason 之后，引导解释它的从句
senses.example: Nobody knows the reason why the birds left so early.
senses.exampleCN: 没人知道这些鸟为什么这么早就离开。
senses.why: The question word becomes a relative word, tying the general noun to its explanation.
senses.whyCN: 这个疑问词变成关系词，把「理由」这个笼统名词与它的解释系在一起。

senses.title: The reason itself
senses.definition: as a noun, the cause or explanation of something, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时指某事的原因或解释，常用复数
senses.example: He never explained the whys of his sudden move.
senses.exampleCN: 他从未解释自己突然搬走的各种原因。
senses.why: A question word was turned into a noun, so the asking itself became the thing asked about.
senses.whyCN: 一个疑问词被变成名词，于是「发问」本身成了被追问的对象。

senses.title: In an exclamation
senses.definition: used at the beginning of an exclamation to express surprise or protest
senses.definitionCN: 放在感叹句开头，表示惊讶或抗议
senses.example: Why, that is the very book I lost last week!
senses.exampleCN: 哎呀，那正是我上星期丢的那本书！
senses.why: The same word softened an objection, and in speech it became a small surprised noise.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词能缓和反驳，在口语中又成了小小的惊讶声。

intro.en: Why descends from Old English hwy, the instrumental case of the question stem, literally by what.
intro.cn: why 源自古英语 hwy，是疑问词干的工具格，字面意思是「凭着什么」。

items.en: The old stem had a case for means or instrument, which answered the question by what agency.
items.cn: 古老的词干有一个表示手段或工具的格，回答「凭借什么」这一问题。

items.en: Hwy and hwi were the instrumental forms, and they were used to ask for a cause.
items.cn: hwy 与 hwi 是工具格形式，用来追问原因。

items.en: The form settled as why, and the word also began to stand after the noun reason.
items.cn: 词形固定为 why，这个词也开始出现在名词 reason 之后。

items.en: Why not became a polite suggestion, and why on earth added force to surprise.
items.cn: why not 成为礼貌的建议，why on earth 则为惊讶加上力量。

items.en: The plural whys turned the question into a noun, as in the whys of a decision.
items.cn: 复数 whys 把提问变成名词，如 the whys of a decision。

note.en: The first group gathers the other question words of the same family, the second the words that give reasons back.
note.cn: 第一组收同族其他疑问词，第二组收给出原因的回答词。

entries.definition: The question word for a thing.
The question word for a person.
The question word for manner, not cause.
The question word for place.
The word that answers a why question.
The explanation a why question looks for.
An old formal word meaning for what reason.

normalIntro.en: Why is a single syllable that always points backwards, from a fact to its cause.
normalIntro.cn: why 是一个总是往回指的音节，从一件事指回它的原因。

normal.en: Why shares its w with what and where, the whole family of questions.
normal.cn: why 与 what、where 共用 w，同属一整个疑问家族。

normal.en: Y is the fork in the road, the point where you ask which way and why.
normal.cn: 字母 y 像岔路口，正好是你问「为什么走这条」的地方。

normal.en: Why not is a yes wearing a question mark.
normal.cn: why not 就是一个戴着问号的「好」。

normal.en: The reason why keeps the question glued to its noun.
normal.cn: the reason why 把问句粘在它的名词后面。

normal.en: The whys of a thing are its reasons, counted up.
normal.cn: 一件事的 whys 就是它的种种缘由，被一条条数出来。

abstract.en: Feel the tug on a sleeve that will not stop.
abstract.cn: 感觉袖子上那一下不肯停的拉扯。

abstract.en: See a cloud that refuses to say where it is going.
abstract.cn: 看见一朵云不肯说它要去哪。

abstract.en: Hear a question that has no floor beneath it.
abstract.cn: 听见一个底下没有地板的问题。

examples.en: Why is the light still on upstairs?
examples.cn: 楼上为什么还亮着灯？

examples.en: I cannot explain why she left so suddenly.
examples.cn: 我无法解释她为什么走得那么突然。

examples.en: Why not ask the teacher to look at it again?
examples.cn: 何不让老师再看一遍呢？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外」——往外看半天也想不通，只好问一句为什么。

root: 日耳曼语疑问词干的工具格（凭何）→ 古英语 hwy → 中古英语 why → 现代英语 why；同族有 what、where、how。

sensesIntro.en: The word asks what led to something, becomes a cheerful suggestion, then a relative word, then the reason itself, and at last a small surprised opening.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词追问是什么引出了某事，接着变成愉快的建议、关系词、原因本身，最后成为一声小小的惊讶。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child pulling a sleeve, asking one question again.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个孩子拉扯袖子，把同一个问题再问一遍。

branches.en: The cause branch: why the train stopped in a field.
branches.cn: 原因分支：火车为何停在田野里。

branches.en: The suggestion branch: why not take the early bus.
branches.cn: 建议分支：何不坐早班车。

branches.en: The linking branch: the reason why the birds left.
branches.cn: 连接分支：鸟早早离开的原因。

branches.en: The noun branch: the whys of a sudden move.
branches.cn: 名词分支：突然搬走的种种原因。

branches.en: The exclamation branch: why, that is my book.
branches.cn: 感叹分支：哎呀，那是我的书。

intro.en: Why is a bare question word with no affixes of its own, and its only derived form is the plural whys.
intro.cn: why 是不带任何词缀的疑问词，它唯一的派生形式是复数 whys。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no Latin source; the Latin entries below show the borrowed relatives such as quare and causa.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目展示 quare、causa 这类借入的相关词。

items.example: It works as adverb and noun.
It softens advice into a question.

items.exampleCN: 这里疑问词变成关系词。

items.example: It carries where plus for, not why.
items.exampleCN: 它由 where 与 for 组成，并非来自 why。

items.example: It adds a tone of disbelief.
items.exampleCN: 它增添难以置信的语气。

items.example: It answers a why with a shrug.
items.exampleCN: 它用一个耸肩回答「为什么」。

latinEntries.example: It is the closest Latin question of cause.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是拉丁语中最接近的原因问词。

definition_zh: 宽的；宽阔的；广泛的；睁大的；差得远的
definition_en: measuring a large distance from one side to the other, and figuratively covering a large range
core_image: 一条从田埂这头一直铺到那头的大河，两岸之间没有桥，只有很宽很宽的河面
scene: 站在河堤上，对岸的树像一条细线，中间的水面宽得望不到边。The river is so wide that the other bank looks like a thin grey line.
sceneCN: 这里 wide 是「宽的」（第 1 个义项：从一边到另一边距离大）；句意为河那么宽，对岸看起来像一条灰细线。那条铺满整个视野、中间没有桥的河面，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 宽的；宽阔的；广泛的；睁大的

senses.title: Large from side to side
senses.definition: measuring a good distance from one side to the other
senses.definitionCN: 从一边到另一边有相当长的距离
senses.example: The river is so wide that the other bank looks like a thin grey line.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河那么宽，对岸看起来像一条灰细线。
senses.why: This physical span is the oldest and most literal sense, and every other use grows from it.
senses.whyCN: 这种物理上的跨度是最古老、最字面的意思，其他用法都从它长出来。

senses.title: Covering a large range
senses.definition: including many different things, kinds or people
senses.definitionCN: 包括许多不同的事物、种类或人
senses.example: The shop sells a wide range of tools and paints.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售种类广泛的工具和油漆。
senses.why: A wide spread covers much ground, and a list of many kinds spreads in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 宽阔的摊开占据大片地面，而涵盖许多种类的清单也是以同样方式铺开的。

senses.title: Fully open
senses.definition: used of eyes or doors that are opened to the full
senses.definitionCN: 形容眼睛或门被完全打开
senses.example: She stared at the letter with wide eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 她睁大眼睛盯着那封信。
senses.why: A fully opened eye is stretched from side to side, so the measurement becomes a state of opening.
senses.whyCN: 完全睁开的眼睛两边拉长，于是这种度量变成了一种打开的状态。

senses.title: Far from the target
senses.definition: used of an answer or a shot that misses by a large distance
senses.definitionCN: 形容答案或射击偏离目标很远
senses.example: His guess was wide of the mark and made everyone laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 他猜得完全不对，把大家都逗笑了。
senses.why: An arrow landing wide of the target is simply far across the field, and the image carried over to answers.
senses.whyCN: 箭落在靶子旁边的宽处，不过是横过大片场地，这一形象又被带到了答案上。

senses.title: Completely, in adverb use
senses.definition: as an adverb, used with open or apart to mean to the full extent
senses.definitionCN: 作副词时与 open、apart 搭配，表示达到最大限度
senses.example: The windows stood wide open all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午窗子都大开着。
senses.why: The adjective took the adverb job because English wants a word that measures the full opening.
senses.whyCN: 形容词承担了副词的工作，因为英语需要一个词来衡量完全打开的程度。

intro.en: Wide comes from Old English wid, from a Germanic root that also gives width, and its first meaning was simply broad.
intro.cn: wide 源自古英语 wid，其日耳曼语词根也给出 width，最初的意思就是「宽阔」。

items.en: The root described something spread out across space, as opposed to long from end to end.
items.cn: 这个词根描述的是一样东西在空间中横向铺开，与「从头到尾的长」相对。

items.en: Wid meant broad and spacious, and the noun widu was already forming beside it.
items.cn: wid 表示宽阔、空旷，旁边已经出现了名词形式。

items.en: The spelling became wide, and the word began to describe range as well as width.
items.cn: 拼写变为 wide，这个词除了宽度也开始描述范围。

items.en: Expressions such as a wide range and wide open extended it from the physical to the abstract.
items.cn: a wide range、wide open 这类说法把它从物理延伸到抽象。

items.en: The adverb use survives mainly in set pairs such as wide open, wide apart and far and wide.
items.cn: 副词用法主要保存在 wide open、wide apart、far and wide 等固定搭配中。

note.en: The first group gathers the other words of measurement, the second the words for a large range or spread.
note.cn: 第一组收其他度量词，第二组收表示范围大、分布广的词。

entries.definition: The measurement itself, from side to side.
To make or become wide.
Living free in nature, a different word.
Measuring a large distance end to end, the other axis.
Wide, often of shoulders, roads or views.
Covering a large area or range.
Extremely wide, almost beyond measuring.

normalIntro.en: Wide is a measurement word, so picture something you could run across rather than turn end for end.
normalIntro.cn: wide 是度量词，所以要想象一样能横着跑过去的东西，而不是把它转一整圈。

normal.en: Wide and long are two axes; a door is wide, and a corridor is long.
normal.cn: wide 与 long 是两条轴：门是宽的，走廊是长的。

normal.en: Wide eyes and wide open share one picture of stretching to the limit.
normal.cn: wide eyes 与 wide open 共用一幅拉到极限的画面。

normal.en: A wide range is the same stretch, filled with kinds instead of metres.
normal.cn: a wide range 是同一种铺开，只是填的不是米，而是种类。

normal.en: Width turns the adjective into a noun by adding th.
normal.cn: width 加 th 就把形容词变成了名词。

normal.en: Far and wide means the span of the whole map.
normal.cn: far and wide 就是整张地图那么大的跨度。

abstract.en: Feel the wind crossing an open valley with nothing to stop it.
abstract.cn: 感觉风横穿开阔山谷，没有任何东西挡它。

abstract.en: See two banks so far apart that a voice would not carry.
abstract.cn: 看见两岸远到喊一声都传不过去。

abstract.en: Feel your eyes stretching at a surprising line.
abstract.cn: 感觉眼睛被一句意外的话撑开。

examples.en: The road is wide enough for two trucks to pass.
examples.cn: 这条路宽得能并排过两辆卡车。

examples.en: The museum offers a wide choice of free tours.
examples.cn: 博物馆提供了种类丰富的免费导览。

examples.en: She left the door wide open behind her.
examples.cn: 她离开时把门大开着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外得」——外面得留出很宽的余地，所以是宽的。

root: 日耳曼语词根（横向铺开）→ 古英语 wid（宽阔）→ 中古英语 wide → 现代英语 wide；同族有 width、widen、widely、widespread。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with the physical span from side to side, spreads to a range of things, to eyes opened fully, to a shot missing by a distance, and finally to the adverbial fully.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从左右之间的物理跨度出发，扩展到事物的范围、睁大的眼睛、偏得很远的射击，最后成为表示「完全」的副词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river so broad that the far bank is only a thin line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条大河宽到对岸只剩一条细线。

branches.en: The river branch: two banks far apart.
branches.cn: 河流分支：两岸相距很远。

branches.en: The range branch: tools and paints of many kinds.
branches.cn: 范围分支：种类繁多的工具与油漆。

branches.en: The eyes branch: staring at a letter.
branches.cn: 眼睛分支：盯着那封信。

branches.en: The miss branch: a guess wide of the mark.
branches.cn: 偏离分支：猜得完全不对。

branches.en: The adverb branch: windows wide open.
branches.cn: 副词分支：窗子大开着。

intro.en: Wide is a free Germanic adjective that builds the noun width, the verb widen and the adverbs widely and wide.
intro.cn: wide 是自由使用的日耳曼语形容词，可派生名词 width、动词 widen 以及副词 widely、wide。

latinIntro.en: The native word has no Latin source; the Latin entries below give the borrowed words often used for breadth and range.
latinIntro.cn: 这个本土词没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目给出常用来表达宽度与范围的借入词。

items.example: It works as adjective and adverb.

items.meaning: in a way, over a range

items.example: The adverb keeps its old breadth.
items.exampleCN: 副词保留了旧日的宽度感。

items.example: The pair spreads the word in two directions.
items.exampleCN: 这一对词把跨度向两个方向拉开。

items.example: It comes from shooting at a mark.

latinEntries.example: It gives English latitude, first width then freedom.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它给出 latitude，先指宽度后指自由。

definition_zh: 妻子；夫人；（旧）妇女
definition_en: the woman a man or woman is married to, seen from the partner s side
core_image: 两只并排挂在门边的结婚戒指照片，框里两个人肩膀挨得很近
scene: 他指着厨房里那位系着围裙的人，说这就是他妻子，然后笑着去洗碗。His wife teaches at the school at the end of our street.
sceneCN: 这里 wife 是「妻子」（第 1 个义项：与之结婚的那位女性，从配偶一方来看）；句意为他妻子在我们街尾那所学校教书。门边并排挂着的合照，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The married partner
senses.definition: the woman to whom a person is married, spoken of from the other partner s side
senses.definitionCN: 一个人与之结婚的女性，从配偶另一方的角度来说
senses.example: His wife teaches at the school at the end of our street.
senses.exampleCN: 他妻子在我们街尾那所学校教书。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense, a role named from the viewpoint of the person married to her.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常意义，是从与她结婚之人的视角命名的一个角色。

senses.title: A woman in old use
senses.definition: in older English, any adult woman, without any link to marriage
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的英语中泛指成年女性，与婚姻无关
senses.example: In Middle English a wife could mean simply a woman of any rank.
senses.exampleCN: 在中古英语里，wife 可以单纯指任何身份的女性。
senses.why: The broad sense is the original one, and it survives today only inside fixed compounds.
senses.whyCN: 这个宽泛的意义才是最初的义项，今天只在固定复合词内部存活。

senses.title: In fixed pairs
senses.definition: used in paired phrases such as husband and wife or man and wife
senses.definitionCN: 用于 husband and wife、man and wife 这类成对说法
senses.example: They were pronounced man and wife before the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在全村人面前被宣布为夫妻。
senses.why: The wedding formula keeps the older style, and the pair sounds like one unit.
senses.whyCN: 婚礼套语保留了更古老的说法，这一对词听起来像一个整体。

senses.title: Inside compounds
senses.definition: used as a second element in words such as housewife and midwife
senses.definitionCN: 作为 housewife、midwife 等词的后项出现
senses.example: His mother had been a housewife for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他母亲做了三十年家庭主妇。
senses.why: Old compounds kept the broad sense of woman, which is why a midwife is not simply a married woman.
senses.whyCN: 古老的复合词保留了「女性」的宽泛意义，所以 midwife 并不只是已婚妇女。

senses.title: In respectful address
senses.definition: in older formal usage, a title for a married woman, often written before her family name
senses.definitionCN: 在旧式正式用法中，作为已婚女性的称谓，常写在姓氏之前
senses.example: The letter began with a greeting to the doctor and his wife.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信开头向医生和他的夫人问候。
senses.why: The title dropped out of most modern use, and the plain noun is now the neutral choice.
senses.whyCN: 这一称谓在现代多数用法中已消失，普通名词成为中性选择。

intro.en: Wife comes from Old English wif, which meant woman in general, not a married one; the narrowing to married partner came later.
intro.cn: wife 源自古英语 wif，本泛指女性而非已婚者，限定为配偶的意义是后来才出现的。

items.en: The root meant woman, and the related word for a male partner was separate.
items.cn: 这个词根意为女性，指男性配偶的词则另有一个。

items.en: Wif meant woman, and wifman and wermann paired a woman and a man as humans.
items.cn: wif 指女性，wifman 与 wermann 则以「人」为后项来指男女。

items.en: Wif narrowed towards married woman, while woman took over the general sense.
items.cn: wif 的词义收窄为已婚女性，泛指的意义由 woman 接手。

items.en: The plural wives kept the old f to v change, the only trace of the older grammar.
items.cn: 复数 wives 保留了 f 变 v 的变化，这是旧语法的唯一痕迹。

items.en: Compounds such as housewife and midwife still carry the older sense of woman.
items.cn: housewife 与 midwife 这类复合词仍带着旧有的「女性」之义。

note.en: The first group gathers the marriage and family words that look close, the second the words for a partner in general.
note.cn: 第一组收形近的婚姻与家庭词，第二组收泛指伴侣的词。

entries.definition: The male partner in the same relationship.
The plural, with f turned to v.
The state of being alive, one letter apart.
A cutting tool, the same f sound.
A partner in marriage, of either sex.
The person one lives with or shares life with.
A woman on her wedding day.

normalIntro.en: Wife has only one irregular point, the plural wives, and one surprising fact, that it once meant woman.
normalIntro.cn: wife 只有一个不规则点，即复数 wives，还有一个意外事实：它原本指「女性」。

normal.en: Wife turns to wives, and so do knife and life.
normal.cn: wife 变 wives，knife 和 life 也一样。

normal.en: Husband and wife is a fixed pair that reads like one word.
normal.cn: husband and wife 是固定一对，读起来像一个词。

normal.en: A midwife helps at births because the old word meant a woman.
normal.cn: midwife 负责接生，因为旧义就是「女性」。

normal.en: The -fe ending is the only sign of the old grammar left.
normal.cn: 这个 -fe 词尾是旧语法留下的唯一迹象。

normal.en: Remember it as a role seen from the partner s side.
normal.cn: 把它记作从配偶那一侧看到的角色。

abstract.en: See two rings hanging side by side by a door.
abstract.cn: 看见两枚戒指并排挂在门边。

abstract.en: Hear a name introduced with one word in front of it.
abstract.cn: 听一个名字前面只加了一个词就被介绍出来。

abstract.en: Feel a shoulder close to another shoulder in an old photo.
abstract.cn: 感觉老照片里一个肩膀紧挨着另一个肩膀。

examples.en: He and his wife have lived here for forty years.
examples.cn: 他和妻子在这里住了四十年。

examples.en: The two of them were man and wife by the end of the day.
examples.cn: 一天结束的时候，他们俩成了夫妻。

examples.en: The old house belonged to the doctor and his wife.
examples.cn: 那所老房子属于医生和他夫人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怀福」——怀里揣着福气的人，就是妻子。

root: 日耳曼语词根（女性）→ 古英语 wif（女人）→ 中古英语 wif（妻子）→ 现代英语 wife；同族有 wives、housewife、midwife。

sensesIntro.en: The word began as woman, narrowed to the married partner, settled in wedding formulas, lived on inside compounds, and faded as a title of address.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词原本指女性，收窄为配偶，固定在婚礼套语里，存活于复合词内部，最后作为称谓逐渐淡出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rings hanging side by side by the same door.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一扇门边并排挂着的两枚戒指。

branches.en: The everyday branch: a teacher at the end of the street.
branches.cn: 日常分支：街尾教书的妻子。

branches.en: The old branch: any woman of any rank.
branches.cn: 旧义分支：任何身份的女性。

branches.en: The wedding branch: pronounced man and wife.
branches.cn: 婚礼分支：被宣布为夫妻。

branches.en: The compound branch: thirty years as a housewife.
branches.cn: 复合词分支：三十年家庭主妇。

branches.en: The title branch: a letter to the doctor and his wife.
branches.cn: 称谓分支：写给医生夫妇的信。

intro.en: Wife is a root noun whose plural is irregular, and it survives inside old compounds where the second place was once open to any word for woman.
intro.cn: wife 是复数不规则的词根名词，它在古老的复合词中仍然存活，那些复合词的后项原本可换成任何表示女性的词。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below give the borrowed words that translate it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目给出用来翻译它的借入词。

items.example: It gives midwife, a woman who helps at birth.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 midwife，即接生的女性。

items.example: The wedding formula of the old style.
The pair reads as one unit.
items.exampleCN: 这一对读来像一个整体。

latinEntries.example: It shows the older broad sense side by side.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它与更宽泛的旧义并立。

definition_zh: 野生的；荒野的；狂热的；失控的；荒凉的
definition_en: living or growing freely in nature without people, and figuratively uncontrolled, violent or very enthusiastic
core_image: 一片没有篱笆的草坡，风一过草就朝同一个方向倒，中间有一条窄窄的兽径
scene: 山坡上没有篱笆、没有人修的路，只有一条被野兽踩出来的窄径，草随风倒向一边。Wild horses still run on this island in summer.
sceneCN: 这里 wild 是「野生的」（第 1 个义项：在自然中自由生长或生活、未经人驯养）；句意为夏天这个岛上仍有野马奔跑。没有篱笆的草坡与那条兽径，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 野生的；无人居住的；狂热的；失控的

senses.title: Living free in nature
senses.definition: used of plants and animals that grow or live without being kept or planted by people
senses.definitionCN: 形容未被人饲养或栽种的动植物
senses.example: Wild horses still run on this island in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天这个岛上仍有野马奔跑。
senses.why: The oldest sense is untamed, which is the state of a creature that no one owns or feeds.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是未被驯服，即没有任何人拥有或喂养的状态。

senses.title: Land without people
senses.definition: used of country that is empty, rough and not farmed or built on
senses.definitionCN: 形容空旷、崎岖、未被耕种或建起的土地
senses.example: Beyond the village there are miles of wild hills.
senses.exampleCN: 村子外面是连绵数里的荒山。
senses.why: An untamed creature needs untamed land, so the word covers the ground as well as its inhabitants.
senses.whyCN: 未经驯服的动物需要未经驯服的土地，于是这个词也覆盖了地面。

senses.title: Out of control
senses.definition: used of behaviour, weather or imagination that runs without restraint
senses.definitionCN: 形容行为、天气或想象失去约束地奔流
senses.example: The crowd went wild when the winning goal went in.
senses.exampleCN: 制胜球进门时，人群发狂了。
senses.why: A wild horse cannot be led, and human feeling that cannot be led takes the same word.
senses.whyCN: 野马牵不动，而牵不动的人的情绪也用同一个词。

senses.title: Very keen on something
senses.definition: in informal use, extremely enthusiastic about a person or activity
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示对某人或某事极度热衷
senses.example: The children are wild about the new cartoon.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们对这部新动画片着迷得不行。
senses.why: Enthusiasm without restraint is another way of being untamed, so the word softened into liking.
senses.whyCN: 不知节制的热情也是未驯服的一种，于是这个词软化成喜欢。

senses.title: Rough and inaccurate
senses.definition: used of a guess or a claim that is made without care or evidence
senses.definitionCN: 形容猜测或断言轻率、没有依据
senses.example: It was only a wild guess, but it turned out right.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是个胡猜，结果竟然猜对了。
senses.why: An arrow shot without aim flies wild, and a guess without aim takes the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 不经瞄准射出的箭会乱飞，不经瞄准的猜测也用这个形容词。

intro.en: Wild comes from Old English wilde, meaning untamed and living in the forest, from a Germanic word for the uncontrolled.
intro.cn: wild 源自古英语 wilde，意为未被驯服、生活在林野之中，其日耳曼语源头与「无约束」有关。

items.en: The root described what was not under human hand, whether a beast or a wood.
items.cn: 这个词根描述不受人手掌控之物，无论野兽还是林子。

items.en: Wilde meant untamed and also described empty, uncultivated land.
items.cn: wilde 表示未被驯服，也描述空旷未耕的土地。

items.en: The word moved from the forest to people, so a wild mood was one without restraint.
items.cn: 这个词从林子移向人，于是 wild mood 指不受约束的情绪。

items.en: Sports writing made go wild the phrase for a crowd losing control.
items.cn: 体育写作让 go wild 成为形容人群失控的说法。

items.en: Casual speech softened it into enthusiasm, as in wild about a band.
items.cn: 口语把它软化为热情，如 wild about a band。

note.en: The first group gathers the closely related wild- words, the second the words for untamed things and land.
note.cn: 第一组收密切相关的 wild- 词族，第二组收表示未驯服之物与土地的词。

entries.definition: Animals and plants living free.
In an uncontrolled way, or very much.
Large land left untamed.
Broad, differing by one sound.
Not made tame or obedient.
Violent and dangerous in attack.
Unprocessed, rough and direct.

normalIntro.en: Wild is a short word with a lot of force, so keep the untamed creature and let the other senses grow from it.
normalIntro.cn: wild 很短却很有力，记住那只未驯服的野兽，其他义项都从它长出来。

normal.en: Wild is the opposite of tame, and a tame horse can be led.
normal.cn: wild 与 tame 相对，而驯服的马是能牵走的。

normal.en: Go wild, run wild, wild guess: all have no rein.
normal.cn: go wild、run wild、wild guess：都没有缰绳。

normal.en: Wild about means keen, the same no-rein energy turned to liking.
normal.cn: wild about 表示热衷，是同一股无缰的劲头变成了喜欢。

normal.en: Wildlife and wilderness both start from this one word.
normal.cn: wildlife 与 wilderness 都从这个词出发。

normal.en: Wild differs from wide only in the final sound.
normal.cn: wild 与 wide 只差最后一个音。

abstract.en: Feel grass bend all the way over in one wind.
abstract.cn: 感觉草被一阵风整个压弯。

abstract.en: See a narrow track made by animals, not people.
abstract.cn: 看见一条由动物而非人踩出的小径。

abstract.en: Hear a crowd roaring louder than the whistle.
abstract.cn: 听见人群的吼声比哨声还响。

examples.en: Wild flowers line the path every spring.
examples.cn: 每年春天小路两边都开满野花。

examples.en: The crowd went wild when the singer appeared.
examples.cn: 歌手出现时人群沸腾了。

examples.en: Beyond the wall the land turns wild and rocky.
examples.cn: 墙那边土地变得荒凉多石。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪的」——长歪了没人管，就变成野生的了。

root: 日耳曼语词根（不受掌控）→ 古英语 wilde（未驯服、荒芜）→ 中古英语 wild → 现代英语 wild；同族有 wildly、wilderness、wildlife。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with a creature no one owns, spreads to land with no people, jumps to feeling without a rein, softens into keen liking, and ends with a guess that has no aim.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从无人拥有的生物出发，扩展到无人的土地，跳到没有缰绳的情绪，软化为热衷，最后落在没有瞄准的猜测上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fenceless slope with one narrow track worn by animals.
core.cn: 核心意象：没有篱笆的草坡，只有一条兽径。

branches.en: The horses branch: wild horses on the island.
branches.cn: 野马分支：岛上的野马。

branches.en: The hills branch: miles of rough empty land.
branches.cn: 山野分支：连绵数里的荒山。

branches.en: The crowd branch: roaring at the winning goal.
branches.cn: 人群分支：制胜球时的怒吼。

branches.en: The fan branch: children and a new cartoon.
branches.cn: 粉丝分支：孩子与新动画。

branches.en: The guess branch: right by accident.
branches.cn: 猜测分支：碰巧猜对。

intro.en: Wild is a free adjective that builds the -ly adverb, the -ness noun and the older noun wilderness, and it heads compounds such as wildlife.
intro.cn: wild 是自由使用的形容词，可派生 -ly 副词、-ness 名词与较古老的 wilderness，还作为前项构成 wildlife 一类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below show the borrowed words for untamed nature.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目展示表示未经驯服之自然的借入词。

items.example: It works as adjective, noun and adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它可作形容词、名词与副词。

items.example: It forms wildly, also meaning very.
The crowd picture in two words.
items.exampleCN: 两个词画出人群的画面。

items.example: It suits children and gardens alike.
items.exampleCN: 它既适合孩子也适合园子。

items.example: The adjective turned noun keeps the land.
items.exampleCN: 形容词转名词后保留了土地之意。

definition_zh: 将；会；愿意；意志；遗嘱
definition_en: the word that marks the future or a decision, and the noun for the power to choose, or for a document about property after death
core_image: 一个人伸手推开一扇沉重的门，手已经按在门上，还没推
scene: 他站在门口，手按在门板上停了一下，然后说他会去把这件事办完。I will call you as soon as the meeting ends.
sceneCN: 这里 will 是「将、会」（第 1 个义项：表示将来或决定）；句意为会议一结束我就给你打电话。那只已经按在门上、还没推开的手，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Marking the future
senses.definition: used with another verb to speak about the future or about what is expected
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个动词连用，谈论将来或预期会发生的事
senses.example: I will call you as soon as the meeting ends.
senses.exampleCN: 会议一结束我就给你打电话。
senses.why: The future use grew out of the older sense of wanting, since what one wants tends to happen next.
senses.whyCN: 将来义从旧的「想要」义长出来，因为人想要的往往是接下来会发生的事。

senses.title: Expressing a decision or promise
senses.definition: used to show a choice just made, a promise or a refusal
senses.definitionCN: 表示刚做出的选择、承诺或拒绝
senses.example: I will not lend him the car again.
senses.exampleCN: 我再也不把车借给他了。
senses.why: Here the word is doing what it did first, putting a wish into a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词做的是它最早的工作：把一个意愿放进句子。

senses.title: The power to choose
senses.definition: the mental power by which a person decides and keeps to a choice
senses.definitionCN: 一个人作出决定并坚持下去的心理力量
senses.example: It took great will to finish the climb in that wind.
senses.exampleCN: 在那样的风里爬完全程需要极大的意志。
senses.why: The noun names the faculty behind every use of the modal, the inner hand on the door.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名了每一个情态用法背后的能力，也就是那只按在门上的手。

senses.title: A document after death
senses.definition: a legal paper saying who should receive a person s property after death
senses.definitionCN: 一份法律文件，说明一个人去世后财产归谁
senses.example: She made a will and left the house to her niece.
senses.exampleCN: 她立了遗嘱，把房子留给侄女。
senses.why: The document states a person s last wishes, so the word for wanting became the word for the paper.
senses.whyCN: 这份文件陈述一个人最后的意思，于是表示「意愿」的词成了文件之名。

senses.title: To make something happen by wanting
senses.definition: in a somewhat formal use, to bring something about by determination, or to leave property by a will
senses.definitionCN: 在稍正式用法中，指凭决心促成某事，或指按遗嘱留下财产
senses.example: He willed himself to stay calm in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 他在大厅里强使自己保持镇定。
senses.why: The noun turned back into a verb, so a person can now will a result or will a house to a friend.
senses.whyCN: 名词又转回动词，于是人可以用意志促成结果，或把房子遗赠给朋友。

intro.en: Will comes from Old English willan, to wish, and the same word served both as noun and as verb from the beginning.
intro.cn: will 源自古英语 willan（希望），从一开始就兼作名词与动词。

items.en: The root meant to wish or to want, and the noun named the wishing itself.
items.cn: 这个词根表示希望、想要，名词则命名这个「希望」本身。

items.en: Willan was the verb of wishing, and willa the noun for a wish or a purpose.
items.cn: willan 是表示希望的动词，willa 是表示愿望或目的的名词。

items.en: The word gained the future use, at first for intention, then for plain prediction.
items.cn: 这个词获得了将来用法，先表示意图，后表示单纯的预测。

items.en: The contraction won’t came from wol not and settled as the negative form.
items.cn: 缩写 won’t 来自 wol not，最终固定为否定形式。

items.en: The legal sense of a will for property dates from the same period and is now the main noun use.
items.cn: 表示财产文件的法律义同出一时代，如今是该名词的主要用法。

note.en: The first group gathers the other ways English marks the future or willingness, the second the nouns for purpose and choice.
note.cn: 第一组收英语中其他表示将来或意愿的形式，第二组收表示目的与选择的词。

entries.definition: The past of will, also a polite form.
Ready to do something, an adjective.
A short form used in speech, close in shape.
In a good way, differing by one letter.
The older future word, now formal or legal.
To want something that may not happen.
What a person means to do.

normalIntro.en: Will is one short word doing three jobs, so remember the picture of the hand on the door and let grammar follow.
normalIntro.cn: will 一个短词担三份工，记住那只按在门上的手，语法自然跟上。

normal.en: Will began as wanting, so willing and wish sit in the same family.
normal.cn: will 原本是「想要」，所以 willing 与 wish 同属一家。

normal.en: I will is both a promise and a future, since a promise is a small future.
normal.cn: I will 既是承诺也是将来，因为承诺就是一个小小的将来。

normal.en: Won’t looks nothing like will, and that odd shape makes it easy to recall.
normal.cn: won’t 看起来和 will 毫无关系，这种奇特形状反而容易记。

normal.en: Free will and will power both count the inner strength.
normal.cn: free will 与 will power 都在数内心的力量。

normal.en: A will for property is simply a person s last wish written down.
normal.cn: 关于财产的 will 就是把一个人最后的心愿写下来。

abstract.en: See a hand resting on a heavy door before the push.
abstract.cn: 看见一只手在推之前先按在沉重的门上。

abstract.en: Hear a promise said with the chin lifted.
abstract.cn: 听见一个抬着下巴说出的承诺。

abstract.en: Feel the effort of not turning back halfway.
abstract.cn: 感觉半路上忍住不回头的那股劲。

examples.en: I will meet you at the station at six.
examples.cn: 我六点在车站接你。

examples.en: She has a strong will and never gives up easily.
examples.cn: 她意志坚强，从不轻易放弃。

examples.en: He left the farm to his son in his will.
examples.cn: 他在遗嘱里把农场留给了儿子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为尔」——为了你才愿意去做，这就是意志与心愿。

root: 日耳曼语词根（希望、想要）→ 古英语 willan（希望）→ 中古英语 will → 现代英语 will；同族有 would、willing、willingly、willingness。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as wanting, serves to mark what will happen, names the power of choice, becomes the paper of last wishes, and finally returns as a verb of determination.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「想要」开始，用来标记将发生之事，命名选择的力量，变成写最后心愿的纸，最后作为表决心的动词回来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a heavy door, not yet pushing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在沉重的门上，还没推开。

branches.en: The future branch: I will call after the meeting.
branches.cn: 将来分支：会后我给你打电话。

branches.en: The refusal branch: I will not lend the car.
branches.cn: 拒绝分支：不再借车。

branches.en: The strength branch: finishing a climb in wind.
branches.cn: 力量分支：顶着风爬完全程。

branches.en: The document branch: the house left to a niece.
branches.cn: 文件分支：房子留给侄女。

branches.en: The effort branch: willing oneself to stay calm.
branches.cn: 努力分支：强使自己保持镇定。

intro.en: Will is a root word with no affixes, and its family grows by -ing forms and by the irregular past would.
intro.cn: will 是不带词缀的词根词，其词族靠 -ing 形式与不规则的过去式 would 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no Latin source; the Latin entries below show the borrowed words about will and testaments.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目展示关于意愿与遗嘱的借入词。

items.example: It works as modal, noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 它可作情态动词、名词与动词。

items.example: An irregular shape from wol not.
items.exampleCN: 由 wol not 而来的不规则形式。

items.example: The noun in a small frame.

latinEntries.example: It gives the English testament and testamentary.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它给出英语的 testament 与 testamentary。

definition_zh: 赢；获胜；赢得；争取到
definition_en: to finish first in a contest, or to gain something by effort, skill or luck
core_image: 终场哨响，记分牌上那个数字压过对方，全队冲到场中央抱成一团
scene: 最后一球落地，记分牌上的数字终于反超，队友全冲进场内抱成一团。Our team won the match by a single point in the final second.
sceneCN: 这里 win 是「赢、获胜」（第 1 个义项：在比赛中拿到第一）；句意为我们在最后一秒以一分优势赢下了比赛。终场那一刻记分牌上的反超，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: To finish first in a contest
senses.definition: to come first or beat the others in a game, race or fight
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、竞赛或战斗中拿第一、胜过其他人
senses.example: Our team won the match by a single point in the final second.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在最后一秒以一分优势赢下了比赛。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply to come out on top, the person or side that stays standing.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是压过对手，留下站着的一方。

senses.title: To gain something by effort
senses.definition: to get something such as a prize, a job or respect through effort or merit
senses.definitionCN: 凭努力或实力得到奖品、职位或尊重
senses.example: She won a scholarship to study abroad after a year of preparation.
senses.exampleCN: 准备了一年之后，她赢得了出国留学的奖学金。
senses.why: A prize follows the contest, so the same verb came to name the thing carried home.
senses.whyCN: 奖品是比赛之后的产物，于是同一个动词也用来命名被带回家的东西。

senses.title: To persuade someone to your side
senses.definition: to succeed in getting people to support or agree with you
senses.definitionCN: 成功让人们支持或同意你
senses.example: His honest answer won over the whole committee.
senses.exampleCN: 他诚实的回答把整个委员会都争取了过来。
senses.why: Support is another kind of contest, and the one who gathers people has again come first.
senses.whyCN: 支持也是一种比赛，把人聚拢过来的那一方同样拿了第一。

senses.title: A victory itself
senses.definition: a success in a game or an election, used as a countable noun
senses.definitionCN: 比赛或选举中的胜利，作可数名词
senses.example: The season ended with four wins and two losses.
senses.exampleCN: 这个赛季以四胜两负结束。
senses.why: Once the verb was settled, the noun simply names the event of coming first.
senses.whyCN: 动词定型之后，名词就直接命名那次拿第一的事件。

intro.en: Win is an Old English verb of struggle: gewinnan meant to fight for and gain, and the noun gewin was toil as much as victory.
intro.cn: win 是古英语中表示争斗的动词：gewinnan 意为争取得来，名词 gewin 既指劳作也指胜利。

items.en: winnan meant to labour and to fight, and gewinnan to gain something by struggle.
items.cn: winnan 表示劳作与争斗，gewinnan 表示通过斗争得到某物。

items.en: The noun gewin first stressed toil and hardship more than triumph.
items.cn: 名词 gewin 起初强调的是辛劳与艰苦，多于荣耀。

items.en: The prefix fell away and win became the plain verb of gaining a victory.
items.cn: 前缀脱落，win 成为表示获取胜利的朴素动词。

items.en: Sports and elections made the contest sense dominant, with win the prize following.
items.cn: 体育与选举让竞赛义占了主导，赢得奖品的说法随之而来。

items.en: The sense of winning people over grew as a political and social phrase.
items.cn: 争取人心这一义项作为政治与社会用语发展起来。

note.en: The first group gathers short words that look or sound like win, the second words for succeeding or gaining.
note.cn: 第一组收形近音近的短词，第二组收表示取胜或获得的词。

entries.definition: The part of a bird used for flying.
Moving air.
An alcoholic drink made from grapes.
A soft silvery metal or a can.
To defeat an opponent in a contest.
To obtain something wanted.
A great and celebrated victory.

normalIntro.en: Win is one of the shortest verbs in the book, so fix it by its sound rather than by spelling tricks.
normalIntro.cn: win 是全书最短的动词之一，靠声音记比靠拼写技巧更可靠。

normal.en: The three letters sit in the middle of winner and winter alike.
normal.cn: 这三个字母在 winner 和 winter 里都处在中间。

normal.en: Past tense won changes the vowel, like sing to sang.
normal.cn: 过去式 won 换了元音，如同 sing 变 sang。

normal.en: W and V are the only difference between win and vine, so round the lips.
normal.cn: win 与 vine 只差在 w 和 v，所以要收圆嘴唇。

normal.en: Win begins with a W for the raised arms of the victor.
normal.cn: win 首字母 w，像胜利者高举的两条手臂。

normal.en: A win can be one point: the smallest margin still counts.
normal.cn: 一分的优势也算赢，最小的差距也作数。

abstract.en: The sound of the final whistle and a burst of shouting.
abstract.cn: 终场哨响，一片爆发出来的喊声。

abstract.en: A hand raised before the result is even read out.
abstract.cn: 结果还没念，手已经举了起来。

abstract.en: The line of the finish ribbon breaking.
abstract.cn: 终点那条彩带被撞断的弧线。

examples.en: They won the cup for the first time in thirty years.
examples.cn: 他们三十年来第一次赢得了那座奖杯。

examples.en: You cannot win every argument.
examples.cn: 你不可能赢下每一场争论。

examples.en: She won the trust of her students within a month.
examples.cn: 她一个月内就赢得了学生的信任。

dict_mnemonic.text: 首字母 W 像两只举起的手臂 —— 赢了才举起来。

root: 古英语 winnan（劳作、争斗）→ gewinnan（争得）→ 中古英语 win；同族有 winner、winnings。

sensesIntro.en: From hard struggle the word narrows to sport, widens to prizes, then to people won over, and finally becomes the victory itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从艰苦的争斗收窄到体育，再扩展到奖品，再扩展到被争取的人，最后成为胜利本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scoreboard that suddenly turns in your favour.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块记分牌忽然转向你这边。

branches.en: The contest branch: a match taken by one point.
branches.cn: 竞赛分支：以一分之差拿下比赛。

branches.en: The prize branch: a scholarship earned through effort.
branches.cn: 奖品分支：凭努力挣来的奖学金。

branches.en: The persuasion branch: a committee brought to your side.
branches.cn: 说服分支：把委员会争取过来。

branches.en: The record branch: four wins in a season.
branches.cn: 记录分支：一个赛季四场胜利。

branches.en: The social branch: winning is done to people as well as against them.
branches.cn: 社会分支：赢既可以对抗人，也可以把人赢过来。

intro.en: Win is a bare Germanic root that takes ordinary endings and forms compounds such as outwin and winnings.
intro.cn: win 是一个光秃秃的日耳曼词根，能接普通词尾，也能构成 outwin、winnings 这类派生词。

latinIntro.en: The root is native and has no Latin source; the Latin entry stands for a borrowed idea only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根是本土的，没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目只是借入的概念。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 winning 和 winnings。

items.example: The verb doubled into a slogan.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词叠成了一个口号。

definition_zh: 风；风力；气息；风声、消息；趋势；（管乐器中的）管乐；使喘不过气；缠绕（读 /waɪnd/）
definition_en: natural air moving across the earth's surface; also breath, a hint of news, a tendency, or to twist something around
core_image: 整片草叶被同一股力量压向一侧，沙粒贴着地面快速爬行，旗面被撑得笔直
scene: 海边的山坡上，草全部向同一方向倒伏，观察者说 The wind bends the grass flat against the hillside.
sceneCN: 这里 wind 指「在地表流动的自然空气」（第 1 个义项：能推动物体、改变植物形态的风）；句意为风把草压得贴向山坡。图中可辨识物件：倒伏的草、旗子、沙粒、远处的海面。

pos.zh: 风；风力；气息；风声；趋势；管乐器（读 /wɪnd/）
缠绕；上发条；使弯曲前进（同形异音，读 /waɪnd/）

senses.title: Natural air in motion
senses.definition: air moving across the surface of the earth, usually named by the direction it comes from
senses.definitionCN: 沿地表流动的空气，通常按来向命名
senses.example: A warm wind came off the desert at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时一阵暖风从沙漠方向吹来。
senses.why: The noun is one of the oldest words in English, and its core is simply air that moves.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是英语最古老的词之一，核心意思不过是「在动的空气」。

senses.title: Force or strength of moving air
senses.definition: the speed or force of the air, often graded on a scale for weather and sailing
senses.definitionCN: 空气的速度或力量，常按天气与航海的分级来衡量
senses.example: The wind reached gale force before the harbour closed.
senses.exampleCN: 港口关闭前，风力已达到大风级。
senses.why: Once wind names the moving air, the same word naturally names how strongly it blows.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 wind 指流动的空气，同一个词自然也能指它吹得有多强。

senses.title: Breath or power to breathe
senses.definition: the ability to breathe easily, especially after effort
senses.definitionCN: 顺畅呼吸的能力，尤指用力之后
senses.example: He stopped at the top of the hill to get his wind back.
senses.exampleCN: 他在山顶停下，好把气缓过来。
senses.why: Breath was thought of as air moving in and out of the body, so the outdoor word was borrowed for the inner one.
senses.whyCN: 呼吸被看作空气在身体里进出，于是户外的词被借去指体内的空气。

senses.title: A hint or rumour
senses.definition: a piece of news or a hint that has begun to spread quietly
senses.definitionCN: 开始悄悄传开的一点消息或暗示
senses.example: The staff got wind of the merger before it was announced.
senses.exampleCN: 员工在合并公布之前就听到了风声。
senses.why: News was imagined as something carried on the air, arriving before any official statement.
senses.whyCN: 消息被想象成随风而来的东西，比正式声明先到。

senses.title: A tendency or force of change
senses.definition: a widespread movement of opinion or events that pushes change in a direction
senses.definitionCN: 推动事情朝某方向改变的普遍舆论或事件趋势
senses.example: The winds of reform reached even the oldest institutions.
senses.exampleCN: 改革之风甚至吹到了最古老的机构。
senses.why: The metaphor makes social change a weather system, with direction and force of its own.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把社会变化变成天气系统，自带方向与力量。

senses.title: Wind instruments
senses.definition: the group of instruments played by blowing air, such as flutes and trumpets
senses.definitionCN: 靠吹气发声的一组乐器，如长笛与小号
senses.example: The wind section entered after the strings faded.
senses.exampleCN: 弦乐渐弱之后，管乐声部进来了。
senses.why: These instruments work by moving air, so players shorten 'wind instruments' to 'the wind'.
senses.whyCN: 这些乐器靠推动空气发声，因此乐手把 wind instruments 缩称为 the wind。

senses.title: To leave someone breathless
senses.definition: to hit or exhaust someone so that they cannot breathe easily for a moment
senses.definitionCN: 撞击或消耗某人，使其一时无法顺畅呼吸
senses.example: The fall winded him for a full minute.
senses.exampleCN: 那一跤让他足足一分钟喘不上气。
senses.why: The verb reverses the breath sense: instead of having wind, a person has it knocked out.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词反转了气息义：人不是有了气，而是气被打掉了。

senses.title: To twist or coil
senses.definition: to wrap something around an object, or to turn a key or handle to make a mechanism work
senses.definitionCN: 把某物绕在物体上，或转动钥匙、手柄使机械运转
senses.example: She wound the old clock every Sunday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每个星期天早上给那座旧钟上发条。
senses.why: This is a different word, pronounced with a long vowel, that happens to share the spelling; its core is turning or coiling.
senses.whyCN: 这是另一个词，读长元音，只是拼写相同；其核心义是转动或盘绕。

intro.en: Wind is a native Germanic noun from Old English wind. Its deeper root is reconstructed, and Latin ventus is a genuine cognate from the same source rather than the origin of the English word. The verb meaning 'to twist' is a separate homograph with a long vowel.
intro.cn: wind 是古英语 wind 传承下来的日耳曼本族名词。其更深词根为重构形式；拉丁语 ventus 是同出该源的真实同源词，而非英语词的来源。意为「缠绕」的动词是另一个同形异音词，读长元音。

items.en: Wind meant 'moving air' and was already the everyday noun for weather; the same form also served for breath.
items.cn: wind 意为「流动的空气」，早已是谈天气的日常名词；同一形式也用于指呼吸。

items.en: The noun goes back to a Germanic form reconstructed as *windaz, with relatives in Dutch wind and German Wind.
items.cn: 这个名词上溯到重构的日耳曼形式 *windaz，在荷兰语 wind 与德语 Wind 中有亲属。

items.en: The usual reconstruction is a root meaning 'to blow', written *h₂weh₁-; it is a reconstructed form, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 通常把词根重构为意为「吹」的 *h₂weh₁-；这是重构形式，不是有记录的实际词。

items.en: Latin ventus 'wind' comes from the same deep root, so it is a cognate; English did not borrow the word from it.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ventus「风」来自同一深层词根，因此是同源词；英语并非从它借入这个词。

items.en: Breath, rumour, tendency and the musical sense are later extensions; their exact first dates are uncertain and should not be given as fixed facts.
items.cn: 呼吸、风声、趋势与音乐义都是后来的延伸；其确切首见年代不确定，不宜当作固定事实。

note.en: Group one holds words that contain wind but mean something else; group two holds actual wind words that differ in strength or setting.
note.cn: 第一组是含有 wind 字样但意思不同的词；第二组是真正表示风、但力度或场合有别的词。

entries.definition: An opening in a wall for light and air, from Old Norse vindauga 'wind-eye'; it is not a form of wind.
entries.definitionCN: 墙上用于透光和通风的开口，来自古诺尔斯语 vindauga「风眼」；它不是 wind 的词形变化。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'exposed to much wind' or 'long-winded'; it is derived from wind, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「多风的」或「话多的」；由 wind 派生，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: The past participle meaning 'left out of breath', from the verb sense of wind.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，意为「被弄得喘不上气」，来自 wind 的动词义。

entries.definition: The participle of the other wind, pronounced with a long vowel: twisting, or following a twisting path.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个 wind 的分词，读长元音：缠绕的，或沿弯曲路径延伸的。

entries.definition: A light, pleasant wind, often from the sea; wind itself can be any strength.
entries.definitionCN: 轻柔宜人的风，常指海风；wind 则可指任何强度。

entries.definition: A very strong wind, especially one graded on the Beaufort scale; it is a level of wind, not a different phenomenon.
entries.definitionCN: 极强的风，尤指蒲福风级中的一级；它是风的一个等级，不是另一种现象。

entries.definition: A sudden short blast of wind; it is a momentary event within a steadier wind.
entries.definitionCN: 突然而短促的一阵风；是较稳定风中的瞬时事件。

entries.definition: A current of cool air inside a building; wind is usually the outdoor weather word.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑内部的冷空气流；wind 通常指户外的天气现象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real native root, a real cognate and real compounds, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的英语本族词根、真实同源词与真实复合词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English wind; the same Germanic stock gives Dutch wind and German Wind.
normal.cn: 古英语 wind；同日耳曼词源给出荷兰语 wind 与德语 Wind。

normal.en: Latin ventus is a cognate, not the source; the two words grew from the same deep root.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ventus 是同源词而非来源；两个词从同一深层词根长出。

normal.en: Compounds mark the uses: wind speed, windmill, windbreak, windward.
normal.cn: 复合词标出用法：风速、风车、防风林、迎风。

normal.en: The phrase 'get wind of' keeps the old image of news arriving on the air.
normal.cn: 「get wind of」保留了消息随风而来的旧意象。

normal.en: Remember the homograph: the twisting verb is wound and winding, not winded.
normal.cn: 记住同形异音词：缠绕义的过去式是 wound、分词是 winding，不是 winded。

abstract.en: Picture a flag pulling so hard that the pole leans with it.
abstract.cn: 想象旗子拉得那么用力，连旗杆都跟着倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour crossing a playground faster than any child can run.
abstract.cn: 想象一则谣言穿过操场，比任何孩子跑得都快。

abstract.en: Picture an old clock key turning in a slow circle until the spring is tight.
abstract.cn: 想象一把旧钟的发条钥匙慢慢转圈，直到弹簧绷紧。

examples.en: The wind tore the awning loose before the storm arrived.
examples.cn: 风暴到来之前，风把遮阳篷扯松了。

examples.en: She stood still until she had her wind again.
examples.cn: 她站住不动，直到气息恢复。

examples.en: The conductor asked the wind to play softer in the second movement.
examples.cn: 指挥要求管乐在第二乐章吹得更轻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「温的」——温的空气一动起来，就成了风

root: 古英语 wind「流动的空气」，属日耳曼语族，可上溯重构形式 *windaz 与意为「吹」的印欧词根 *h₂weh₁-（重构形式）。拉丁语 ventus 为同源词而非来源。意为「缠绕」的动词是同形异音词，读 /waɪnd/，与本条名词不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: air in motion is first weather, then its strength, then the breath inside a body, then news and social change carried on the air, then the instruments that use it, and finally two verbs, one about breath and one about twisting.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线索展开：运动的空气先是天气，再是它的强度，然后是体内的气息，再是随风传播的消息与社会变化，然后是借空气发声的乐器，最后是两个动词，一个关于气息，一个关于缠绕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grass bent flat in one direction while sand skims the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：草被压得倒向一侧，沙粒贴着地面飞掠。

branches.en: WEATHER: the moving air and the strength with which it blows.
branches.cn: 天气：流动的空气与它吹出的力量。

branches.en: BREATH IN AND OUT: having wind, and having it knocked away.
branches.cn: 气息进出：有气，与气被打掉。

branches.en: AIRBORNE NEWS: rumours and reform both travel like weather.
branches.cn: 随风的消息：谣言与改革都像天气一样传播。

branches.en: BLOWN INSTRUMENTS: music made by moving air through a tube.
branches.cn: 吹奏乐器：让空气穿过管子而发声。

branches.en: THE HOMOGRAPH: a separate verb of turning and coiling, pronounced long.
branches.cn: 同形异音词：另一个表示转动与盘绕的动词，读长元音。

intro.en: Wind is a free native root that takes -y, -less, -ward and joins compounds such as windmill and windbreak; a separate homograph wind 'to twist' adds wound and winding.
intro.cn: wind 是自由的本族词根，可加 -y、-less、-ward，并与 windmill、windbreak 等构成复合词；另有同形异音词 wind「缠绕」，给出 wound 与 winding。

latinIntro.en: Latin ventus 'wind' is a cognate from the same deep root, and ventosus 'windy' belongs to that Latin family; neither is the source of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ventus「风」是同出深层词根的同源词，ventosus「多风的」属于该拉丁词族；两者都不是英语词的来源。

items.example: The wind rose with the tide.

items.meaning: to twist, coil or turn a key
items.example: Wind the string around the spool.
The ridge is windy even in summer.
The lake lay windless at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 黎明时湖面一丝风也没有。

items.meaning: on the side the wind blows from
items.example: The windward slope gets more rain.

items.meaningCN: 风力驱动的磨坊或风车

items.meaning: a row of trees or a barrier that blocks wind
items.example: The poplar windbreak protects the orchard.
items.exampleCN: 白杨防风林保护着果园。

items.meaningCN: 受风侵袭的；被风吹得光秃的
items.example: A windswept headland faced the sea.
items.exampleCN: 一片受风的岬角面向大海。

latinEntries.structure: ventus, venti (m., second declension; cognate, not source)

definition_zh: 窗户；窗口；（电脑）窗口；橱窗；可用的时机
definition_en: an opening in a wall fitted with glass that lets in light and air, and a framed area on a screen
core_image: 雨夜里，窗玻璃上挂满水珠，屋里那盏灯把窗框照成一块发亮的方格
scene: 雨下了整夜，玻璃上挂满水珠，屋里那盏灯把窗框照成一个暖黄的方格。Someone tapped softly on the window while the class was reading.
sceneCN: 这里 window 是「窗户」（第 1 个义项：墙上装玻璃、透光通风的开口）；句意为全班读书时，有人轻轻敲了敲窗户。雨夜里那块被灯光照亮的方格，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 窗户；窗口；橱窗；（电脑）窗口；时机

senses.title: The opening in a wall
senses.definition: a hole in a wall filled with glass and a frame, letting in light and letting you look out
senses.definitionCN: 墙上镶玻璃与框的洞口，可以透光也可以向外看
senses.example: Someone tapped softly on the window while the class was reading.
senses.exampleCN: 全班读书时，有人轻轻敲了敲窗户。
senses.why: The old word named the opening itself, before glass was common, so the hole came first and the pane later.
senses.whyCN: 古词命名的是这个洞口本身，那时玻璃还不普遍，所以先有洞后有玻璃。

senses.title: A shop display area
senses.definition: the large glass front of a shop where goods are shown to the street
senses.definitionCN: 商店朝向街道的大玻璃面，用来展示商品
senses.example: The baker arranged the window before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 面包师在日出前就摆好了橱窗。
senses.why: A shop window does the same job as a house window, showing what lies inside.
senses.whyCN: 商店橱窗与房屋窗户做的是同一件事：展示里面的东西。

senses.title: A framed area on a screen
senses.definition: a box on a computer screen that holds a separate program or document
senses.definitionCN: 电脑屏幕上承载某个程序或文件的一块方形区域
senses.example: She dragged the window to the second screen.
senses.exampleCN: 她把窗口拖到了第二块屏幕上。
senses.why: Early systems offered a peephole into part of the machine, just as a wall window shows part of the world.
senses.whyCN: 早期系统只是给机器内部开了一个窥视孔，正如墙上的窗只展示世界的一部分。

senses.title: A short period for action
senses.definition: a limited stretch of time in which something can still be done, as in a window of opportunity
senses.definitionCN: 还能做某事的有限一段时间，如「机会之窗」
senses.example: The launch window closes on Friday at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 发射窗口在周五中午关闭。
senses.why: Like a window that is open only briefly, a chance admits action for a little while and then shuts.
senses.whyCN: 正如窗户只开一会儿，一次机会也只在短暂时间里放行行动，然后关上。

intro.en: Window is Old Norse: vindauga joins vindr, wind, and auga, eye, so the word literally means wind-eye.
intro.cn: window 来自古诺斯语：vindauga 由 vindr（风）与 auga（眼）组成，字面意思是「风之眼」。

items.en: vindauga meant a wind eye, an unglazed opening that let air into the hall.
items.cn: vindauga 意为风之眼，是让空气进屋的无玻璃开口。

items.en: The native word for such an opening was eyethurl, eye hole, replaced later by the Norse word.
items.cn: 本土表示这种开口的词是 eyethurl（眼洞），后来被诺斯语词取代。

items.en: The form became windowe, still naming the hole rather than the glass.
items.cn: 形式变为 windowe，指的仍是洞口而不是玻璃。

items.en: The spread of glass panes made the window a bright sheet you look through.
items.cn: 玻璃窗格的普及让窗户变成一片透亮的、可望向外的面。

items.en: Computers borrowed the image for the framed area on a screen, and the idea of a brief period gave a window of opportunity.
items.cn: 计算机借用了这个形象来表示屏幕上的方框，而「短暂时期」的想法带来了机会之窗。

note.en: The first group holds parts of a house near a window, the second words for an opening or a chance.
note.cn: 第一组收房屋里与窗相邻的部位，第二组收表示开口或机会的词。

entries.definition: The coldest season of the year.
A woman whose husband has died.
To make or become wider.
Twisting; a bend in a road.
A hole or gap that lets things through.
A moment that may be used for gain.
A showing of goods or work for others to see.

normalIntro.en: Window comes from wind plus eye, and that picture is the fastest way to keep both the meaning and the double consonants.
normalIntro.cn: window 来自 wind 加 eye，这个画面既能记住意思，也能记住那两个辅音。

normal.en: Wind plus eye: the eye of the wind looking into a room.
normal.cn: wind 加 eye：风的眼睛望进屋子。

normal.en: Two letters after the w: wind, then the rest.
normal.cn: w 之后先写 wind，再写剩下的部分。

normal.en: Both o and w are round, like the round pane of an old cottage.
normal.cn: o 和 w 都是圆的，像老屋那扇圆玻璃。

normal.en: A window lets you look out and lets the wind in, two directions at once.
normal.cn: 窗户让你向外看，也让风向内进，同时朝两个方向。

normal.en: Add sill and you get the ledge below, where cats sit patiently.
normal.cn: 加上 sill 就是下面的窗台，猫在那里耐心地坐着。

abstract.en: Cold glass under a fingertip, colder than the room.
abstract.cn: 指尖下的玻璃冰凉，比屋里更冷。

abstract.en: Rain sliding down while the lamp stays steady behind it.
abstract.cn: 雨往下滑，而灯在它后面稳稳地亮着。

abstract.en: A square of light thrown onto the garden path.
abstract.cn: 一片方块的光落在花园小径上。

examples.en: Please close the window before you go to bed.
examples.cn: 睡前请把窗户关上。

examples.en: From my window I can see the whole valley.
examples.cn: 从我的窗户能看到整个山谷。

examples.en: The singer stood in the shop window, drawing a small crowd.
examples.cn: 歌手站在商店橱窗里，引来一小群人。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 非词源玩笑
dict_mnemonic.text: wind（风）+ eye（眼）—— 风的眼睛，就是墙上那个进风透光的「窗户」。

root: 古诺斯语 vindauga（风之眼，vindr 风 + auga 眼）→ 中古英语 windowe → window；同族有 windowsill、windowless。

sensesIntro.en: The noun begins as a hole for wind, becomes a bright pane of glass, then a shop display, a screen box and a short season of opportunity.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词从让风通过的洞开始，变成一片明亮的玻璃，再变成商店陈列、屏幕方框，最后成了短暂的机会期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit square of glass in a dark wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗墙上的一块发亮方格玻璃。

branches.en: The house branch: knuckles tapping on the classroom glass.
branches.cn: 房屋分支：指节轻敲教室玻璃。

branches.en: The trade branch: goods arranged for the street.
branches.cn: 商业分支：摆给街道看的商品。

branches.en: The screen branch: a document moved to another display.
branches.cn: 屏幕分支：文件被挪到另一块显示屏。

branches.en: The time branch: a launch window that shuts at noon.
branches.cn: 时间分支：正午关闭的发射窗口。

branches.en: The metaphor branch: every later sense keeps the idea of a brief opening.
branches.cn: 隐喻分支：后面每个义项都保留了「短暂开口」的想法。

intro.en: Window is a compound of the Norse words for wind and eye; its endings build a small family such as windows and windowless.
intro.cn: window 是诺斯语「风」与「眼」两个词组成的复合词，它的词尾构成 windows、windowless 等一小族词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Scandinavian, not Latin; fenestra, the Latin word for a window, survives in technical adjectives only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自斯堪的纳维亚语而非拉丁语；拉丁语的 fenestra（窗）只残留在技术性形容词里。

items.example: The first half of the Norse original.
The second half, an opening that sees.
items.exampleCN: 后半，一只用于看的开口。

items.example: The body part named by its place.

items.meaning: the glass front of a shop
a short period when action is possible
items.example: The opening sense carried into time.

definition_zh: 葡萄酒；酒；果酒；（引申）令人陶醉之物
definition_en: an alcoholic drink made from fermented grapes or other fruit, and by extension anything that intoxicates
core_image: 烛光里一只高脚杯轻轻一晃，深红的液体贴上杯壁又缓缓流回去
scene: 节日的餐桌上，主人给每只高脚杯倒上深红的酒，烛光在杯壁上一晃一晃。A bottle of red wine was opened to celebrate the harvest.
sceneCN: 这里 wine 是「葡萄酒」（第 1 个义项：用葡萄发酵制成的酒）；句意为开了一瓶红葡萄酒来庆祝丰收。烛光里那只杯壁上深红的液体，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The drink of crushed grapes
senses.definition: an alcoholic drink made by letting grape juice ferment, kept in bottles and served with meals
senses.definitionCN: 让葡萄汁发酵而成的酒，装在瓶里，佐餐饮用
senses.example: A bottle of red wine was opened to celebrate the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 开了一瓶红葡萄酒来庆祝丰收。
senses.why: The word first named the vine itself and its juice, and the drink kept the name as the products spread.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初指葡萄藤及其汁液，随着这些产物传播，饮品保留了名字。

senses.title: Fruit drinks of the same kind
senses.definition: a similar fermented drink made from other fruits, such as plum, apple or pear
senses.definitionCN: 用李子、苹果、梨等其他水果发酵而成的同类饮品
senses.example: Grandmother made pear wine in a big jar every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母每年秋天都用大罐子酿梨酒。
senses.why: Once wine meant fermented fruit juice, any fruit could fill the bottle without changing the word.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 wine 表示发酵果汁，任何水果都能装进这只瓶子而不改词。

senses.title: Something that intoxicates
senses.definition: in literature, anything that lifts the mind like drink, such as joy, praise or freedom
senses.definitionCN: 在文学中，指像酒一样让人心飘起来的东西，如喜悦、赞美或自由
senses.example: The wine of first love made him deaf to all advice.
senses.exampleCN: 初恋这杯酒让他听不进任何劝告。
senses.why: The physical warmth of drink became a picture for any strong feeling that carries reason away.
senses.whyCN: 酒带来的那点身体的暖，成了任何强得足以带走理智的情感的样子。

intro.en: Wine is one of Europe's oldest loanwords: Latin vinum stood behind Old English win well before England had vineyards.
intro.cn: wine 是欧洲最古老的借词之一：早在英格兰有葡萄园之前，拉丁语 vinum 就已经站在古英语 win 的背后。

items.en: vinum meant wine, and the word travelled with Roman traders and soldiers.
items.cn: vinum 意为葡萄酒，这个词随罗马商人与士兵一路传播。

items.en: The Germanic tribes borrowed it early, giving forms such as wīn before any written record.
items.cn: 日耳曼部落很早就借入了它，在有文字记录之前就出现了 wīn 这样的形式。

items.en: win named the drink as well as the vine, and appears in laws on trade and feasts.
items.cn: win 既指饮品也指葡萄藤，出现在关于贸易与宴会的法令里。

items.en: Wine settled into the spelling with a silent e, and became the common word at table.
items.cn: 中古英语时拼写加上不发音的 e，成为餐桌上常用的词。

items.en: The word widened to other fruit drinks and lent its warmth to poetry about joy and love.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到其他果酒，并把它的暖意借给了关于喜悦与爱的诗。

note.en: The first group collects spirits and drinks that look or sound similar, the second beverages and the vine.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的酒与饮品，第二组收饮料与葡萄藤相关的词。

entries.definition: The plant that bears grapes.
Air moving across the land.
To come out on top.
A long high complaining sound.
An alcoholic drink made from grain.
Strong distilled drink.
The fruit from which wine is pressed.

normalIntro.en: Wine is short but often confused with vine; the missing first letter is the whole story of a drink made from a vine.
normalIntro.cn: wine 很短，却常与 vine 混；少掉的那个首字母，正是「藤上长出来的酒」的故事。

normal.en: Vine is the plant, and wine is what the plant becomes once pressed.
normal.cn: vine 是藤，wine 是藤被压榨之后变成的东西。

normal.en: The silent e stays quiet, as in fine and line.
normal.cn: 末尾的 e 不发音，和 fine、line 一样。

normal.en: Wine begins with w for the round top of a glass in profile.
normal.cn: wine 以 w 开头，像侧看的杯口那道弧线。

normal.en: One glass of red, two of white: both keep the same short word.
normal.cn: 一杯红的，两杯白的，用的都是这同一个短词。

normal.en: Wine and dine is a rhyme pair you can hear across a dinner table.
normal.cn: wine and dine 是一对押韵的说法，在餐桌那头都听得见。

abstract.en: Deep red liquid clinging to the inside of a glass.
abstract.cn: 深红的液体贴在杯壁内侧。

abstract.en: The small pop of a cork and a burst of dark scent.
abstract.cn: 软木塞一声轻响，涌出一阵深色的香气。

abstract.en: A voice warming up two chairs further along.
abstract.cn: 隔了两个座位，有个人的声音变暖了。

examples.en: They drank a little wine with the fish.
examples.cn: 他们吃鱼时喝了一点葡萄酒。

examples.en: This wine is made from apples rather than grapes.
examples.cn: 这种酒是用苹果而不是葡萄做的。

examples.en: The village has been making wine for four hundred years.
examples.cn: 这个村子酿酒已有四百年。

dict_mnemonic.text: vine（藤）少一个字母、换个首音就成了 wine —— 藤上结的果子酿成「葡萄酒」。

root: 拉丁语 vinum（葡萄酒）→ 日耳曼语借入 wīn → 古英语 win → 中古英语 wine；同族有 vine、winery、winegrower。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the fermented juice of grapes, widens to other fruits, and finally becomes a picture for anything that makes the heart light.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从发酵的葡萄汁开始，扩展到其他水果，最后成为一切让心变轻之物的图画。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: red liquid turning slowly against a candlelit glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：烛光里深红液体在杯中慢慢打转。

branches.en: The table branch: a bottle opened for the harvest.
branches.cn: 餐桌分支：为丰收开瓶。

branches.en: The orchard branch: pear wine in a big jar.
branches.cn: 果园分支：大罐子里的梨酒。

branches.en: The poetic branch: first love as a drink.
branches.cn: 诗意分支：初恋如一杯酒。

branches.en: The material branch: whatever fruit is available fills the bottle.
branches.cn: 材料分支：有什么果子就装什么瓶子。

branches.en: The extension branch: taste first, then the mind.
branches.cn: 延伸分支：先是舌头，后是心。

intro.en: Wine is a borrowed stem that builds few but useful compounds: winery, wineglass and the verb wine and dine.
intro.cn: wine 是借入的词干，构成的复合词不多但很实用：winery、wineglass，以及 wine and dine 这一说法。

latinIntro.en: The whole word family goes back to Latin vinum, so the Latin column here is the true source, not a cousin.
latinIntro.cn: 整个词族都回到拉丁语 vinum，所以这里的拉丁栏是真正的来源，而不是远亲。
